sections.heading: Tonight (10 minutes)
items: Freeze your credit at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. Save the three logins somewhere safe.
Pick a family safe word and tell your family out loud, not by text.
Turn on transaction alerts for every bank account and card.

sections.heading: Your phone and email
items: Set a carrier account PIN and turn on number lock or port-out protection.
Give your email a long, unique password and its strongest sign-in option.
Switch bank and email logins from text codes to passkeys or an authenticator app where offered.

sections.heading: The three rules
items: Never read a one-time code to anyone who contacted you.
Urgent call about money? Hang up and call back on a number you look up yourself.
Nobody real asks for gift cards, wires, payment apps to strangers, or crypto. Ever.

sections.heading: If it happens
items: Call your bank or card issuer first, using the number on the card.
Report at ReportFraud.ftc.gov, and at IdentityTheft.gov if your identity was used.
Ignore anyone offering to recover your money for a fee: that's the next scam.
